fixtureChunks.content: 1. In this synthetic instrument, “record” means a stored notice and its receipt timestamp.

1. This instrument applies only to operators offering the notice service to the public.
Private household use is outside this scope.

1. The retention duty in Article 5 does not apply to a temporary test record.
This exception does not remove the in-person duty in Article 6.

1. For the duty in Article 5, read “record” as defined in Article 1, within Article 2 and subject to Article 3.
a) The receipt timestamp begins the retention period.
A receipt timestamp is recorded when the notice is received, not when it is drafted.

a) The receipt timestamp begins the retention period.
A receipt timestamp is recorded when the notice is received, not when it is drafted.

1. An operator within Article 2 must retain each record for 7 days, subject to Article 3.
a) Keep the notice text with its receipt timestamp.
b) Preserve the notice text without removing its limiting language.
a) Keep the notice text with its receipt timestamp.
b) Preserve the notice text without removing its limiting language.

1. The operator must appoint a person to attend the annual public information session in person.
Attendance is recorded in the session register maintained by the organizer.
